title: Leave out what the lesson doesn't teach
statement: Leave out anything the lesson does not teach or use, however interesting or familiar, above all at the start: irrelevant material lowers recall and transfer.
example: Excluding extraneous material improves multimedia learning, with a median effect of about 0.70 standard deviations.
detail: An intro-video BrainLift for a Grade 3 reading course records two findings: interesting but irrelevant details reduced recall and transfer and did the most damage at the start of a text (Harp and Mayer 1998), and excluding extraneous material improves multimedia learning, median effect near d 0.70 (Mayer's coherence principle, with Sundararajan and Adesope 2020) (`downloads/BrainLift - What makes a good intro video.md`, lines 129 and 130). Two version-3 inference lesson designs for the course apply it to a familiar reminder: the five story-pattern labels were deleted from the reading-goal panel because the pattern is not taught in that lesson (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.1 - Fantasy Classics - Lesson Designs/3.1 - 2. Aladdin and the Wonderful Lamp, Part 2 (FICTION, INFER) — v3 (new INFER design).docx`, line 54 of its text; `downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/3.1 - Fantasy Classics - Lesson Designs/3.1 - 10. The Wind in the Willows, Part 3 (FICTION, INFER) — v3 (new INFER design).docx`, line 46). The source names Sundararajan and Adesope without a link; its DOI was found on Crossref.
against: The course's lesson-components spec still shows the story-pattern labels as a visual reminder (`downloads/5. Curriculum/Instruction/2. Example lesson structure/Example Lesson Components.docx`, line 11 of its text).
